If the target is already log-scale, evaluate if a power transform (like Yeo-Johnson) provides better normality.

This ensures the model doesn't treat the larger magnitude descriptors as being inherently more significant.

While similar to Morgan fingerprints, MACCS keys represent the presence of specific chemical substructures (like 'is there a carbonyl group?') and can provide complementary information for property prediction.

backlog.spec: Change the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 1. This reduces the feature space significantly and focuses the model on immediate local environments around atoms. This is a 'simpler is better' approach to see if the model is over-fitting on larger, noisier substructures.
backlog.title: Reduce Morgan Fingerprint Radius to 1

backlog.spec: Add the 'max_depth' parameter to the RandomForestRegressor (e.g., max_depth=15). The current model allows trees to grow as deep as necessary until leaves are pure, which can lead to overfitting on small datasets. Limiting the depth can improve generalization.

backlog.spec: Add the 'max_samples' parameter to RandomForestRegressor, setting it to 0.8. This forces each tree to be trained on a bootstrap sample of the data, increasing the diversity between trees and potentially reducing the variance of the ensemble.

backlog.spec: Implement a simple target smoothing or 'shrinkage' toward the mean. Before training, calculate the mean of train_y and adjust the target values: y_new = 0.9 * y + 0.1 * mean(y). This can act as a regularizer to prevent the model from making extreme predictions on outlier molecules.

The final prediction should be the simple average of the three models' outputs. This is a robust way to reduce variance without the overhead of a full stack.

backlog.spec: Before training, calculate the correlation matrix of the 8 RDKit descriptors. If any two descriptors are highly correlated (e.g., > 0.9), remove one of them from the featurize function. This reduces multi-collinearity which can sometimes confuse tree-based models or lead to unstable splits.
backlog.title: High-Variance Decorrelation

backlog.spec: Apply a log1p transformation to the training targets (train_y) before training the model and apply the inverse transformation (expm1) to the predictions. This is intended to stabilize the variance of the regression target.
backlog.title: Log-transform target (y = log1p(y))

backlog.spec: Apply StandardScaler from sklearn to the 8 RDKit descriptors before concatenating them with the Morgan fingerprints. Since Morgan bits are binary and descriptors are continuous, scaling the descriptors might improve the model's ability to weigh them correctly.
backlog.title: Standardize RDKit Descriptors

backlog.spec: Apply MaxAbsScaler to the RDKit descriptors before concatenating with Morgan fingerprints. This scales the descriptors to a [-1, 1] range while preserving sparsity/structure, potentially better than standard scaling for fingerprints.
backlog.title: MaxAbsScaler for Descriptors

backlog.spec: Set a hard limit on the maximum depth of the trees in the RandomForestRegressor (e.g., max_depth=15). This prevents the trees from becoming too complex and over-fitting to noise in the small dataset.
backlog.title: Random Forest with Max Depth Control

backlog.spec: Add a small amount of Gaussian noise (e.g., mean=0, std=0.01) to the training targets to act as a regularizer. This can help the model generalize better by preventing it from fitting the exact values too closely.
backlog.title: Target Smoothing (Gaussian Noise)

backlog.spec: Calculate the correlation of each of the 8 RDKit descriptors with the target. Only include the descriptors in the final feature vector if their absolute correlation with the target is above a certain threshold (e.g., 0.05).
backlog.title: Correlation-based Feature Selection

backlog.spec: Instead of predicting the absolute log-scale permeability, train the model to predict the residual (y - mean(y)). This can sometimes simplify the mapping the model needs to learn.
backlog.title: Predicting Difference from Mean

backlog.spec: Sort the training data by a property (e.g., MolWt) and apply a simple moving average to the targets to smooth out local noise before training.
backlog.title: Target Smoothing (Moving Average)

backlog.spec: Identify the top 3 features with the highest variance and standard deviation. If they are highly correlated with each other, remove the one with the lower correlation to the target to reduce redundancy.
backlog.title: High-Variance Decorrelation

incumbent.description: Quantile Regression Forest approximation: predict the median of the per-tree RF predictions instead of their mean, which may suit the MAE objective.

memo:
Helped: adding RDKit physchem descriptors to Morgan bits (0.4417 to 0.3911, far above the 0.0037 noise). Taking the median of per-tree RF predictions also helped (0.3861, then 0.3794 on replication). The incumbent mean_adjusted is 0.3828.

Did not help: model swaps (XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, ExtraTrees, stacking, GBR), RF tuning (min leaf 2: 0.3929; max_features 0.1: 0.3889; 1000 trees: 0.3865; max depth cap: 0.3898), Morgan radius 3 (0.3972), descriptor interactions (0.3965), extra count features (0.3928), VarianceThreshold (0.3875) and an RF+median blend (0.3850).

Borderline: MACCS keys (0.3792/0.3779 and 0.3792/0.3771) and Morgan radius 1 (0.3822). These are small gains that sit near the noise. Their combination is worth a try, such as radius 1 plus MACCS.

Next: features. Try the full RDKit descriptor set, count fingerprints, fewer Morgan bits, and a target transform. Avoid more model-family swaps.
